metadata.title: David Kinuthia — AI & product engineering consultant
metadata.description: Consulting and contract engineering for teams shipping AI where mistakes are expensive: AI integration, private AI deployments, agentic automation, infrastructure rescue, and fractional CTO support.

home.heroTitle: AI & product engineering consultant - closing the gap between a strong idea and software that ships.
home.heroBody: I help founders and engineering leaders ship AI features, full-stack products, and the infrastructure behind them, with one accountable owner from architecture to the last pixel. I'm based in Nairobi and work with teams around the world.
home.heroAvailability: Engagements range from focused one-to-three-week sprints to multi-quarter builds, plus fractional CTO retainers for founders who need senior technical judgment on call.
home.assessmentLink: Not sure where to start? Take the fit assessment

about.title: About
about.identity: I'm a product engineer who owns problems end-to-end. Over eight years shipping across frontend, backend, integrations, infrastructure, and AI, I've learned that the best work starts with sharper questions—not a longer backlog.
about.edge: Clients bring me in where technical depth meets product judgment: scoping ambiguous work, building MVPs they can learn from, integrating AI into systems that already matter, and hardening platforms as they grow. I own the problem end-to-end, so you get progress, not another person to manage.
about.personal: Outside of code, I recharge by running, reading about how teams build, and chasing good coffee with friends.

work.title: Track record
work.intro: My consulting practice is new, so you won't find client case studies here yet. What you will find is the work I've owned over eight years inside product teams — as engineer, lead, and Head of Engineering — written up the way I'd report on an engagement. These were employers, not clients, and details are kept at a level that respects their confidentiality.

churpy.meta: Fullstack Engineer → Lead Product Engineer → Head of Engineering
churpy.context: Kenyan fintech providing virtual accounts, M-Pesa collections and payouts, ledgers, and finance tooling for businesses.

recon.title: AI-native reconciliation platform
recon.problem: Finance teams matched bank statements against cashbooks, and remittances against invoices, on a legacy microservice workflow that was slow to configure and hard to change.
recon.approach: Rebuilt it from the ground up as a single application: multi-engine PDF and OCR extraction, optimal one-to-many matching, and mailbox, SharePoint, and SFTP connectors. Claude proposes column mappings and match rules and explains exceptions, while matching, quality gates, report math, and approvals stay deterministic, with maker-checker sign-off.
recon.result: AI speeds up setup without ever making the decision. Only small samples reach the model, every AI feature falls back to heuristics when the model is unavailable, and each suggestion is audit-logged. Backed by roughly 310 backend tests.

docsAi.title: Private document Q&A with citations
docsAi.problem: Teams needed answers from large, sensitive document collections without trusting an AI that could invent its sources.
docsAi.approach: Built a retrieval system on Postgres with pgvector and locally generated embeddings. Claude must cite a source for every sentence, and each citation opens the original page with the passage highlighted. A Microsoft Teams version answers from SharePoint, also with citations.
docsAi.result: Answers people can verify in one click, running on infrastructure the team controls and provisioned with Terraform.

akountable.title: Finance platform for small businesses
akountable.problem: Small businesses in Kenya juggled payments, invoicing, payroll, and tax compliance across disconnected tools.
akountable.approach: Started the Vue and TypeScript frontend from scratch and wrote most of it, plus a large share of the Django backend: M-Pesa collections and payouts, KRA eTIMS tax compliance, invoicing, approvals, multi-branch inventory, and payroll.
akountable.result: One product covering everything from payments to payroll. I later hardened the Go payments API with idempotency keys and callback deduplication, so retried payment requests are never processed twice.

infra.title: Cloud migration from AWS to self-managed Kubernetes
infra.problem: Production ran on managed AWS Kubernetes at a cost and complexity out of step with the company's stage.
infra.approach: Wrote all of the roughly 27 Helm charts covering every service, plus Terraform, cert-manager for TLS, External Secrets, Prometheus and Grafana monitoring, and a self-hosted container registry, then moved production to a single self-managed cluster on Hetzner.
infra.result: Production cut over in June 2026, and the cluster's worker nodes later dropped from nine to five.

productNotes.context: Product operations platform that automates the analysis of user feedback for product teams.

main.title: AI insights for product managers
main.problem: Product managers spent hours pulling feedback out of a dozen tools before they could make a decision.
main.approach: Built an AI-driven insights tool in React and Next.js with more than ten integrations, including OpenAI, Notion, Jira, Salesforce, Slack, Figma, Miro, Zapier, and Google Workspace, plus real-time analytics dashboards.
main.result: Analysis time for product managers fell by 30%, and the dashboards lifted user engagement by 40%.

apollo.context: Developer tooling for evaluating and improving AI models, including the open-source ModsysML toolbox.

main.title: LLM management and evaluation tooling
main.problem: Teams choosing and tuning models had no single place to compare them or trust the results.
main.approach: Built a unified LLM management dashboard in React and Next.js, an improved sentiment-analysis module in Python and Django for trust-and-safety work, and interactive docs and onboarding. Contributed to ModsysML, an open-source toolbox for evaluating model responses against test cases.
main.result: Model selection became 30% faster, sentiment-analysis accuracy improved by 25%, and developer setup time dropped by 20%.

twende.context: Mobility startup behind Kenya's first carpooling web app.

main.title: From carpooling to a pandemic pivot
main.problem: The product only existed on Android, and when COVID-19 hit, the business needed a new line of revenue fast.
main.approach: Built the carpooling web app in React, Node.js, and Python, then led the rapid build of a logistics web app with authentication, payments, and order management. Grew from junior engineer to team lead, mentoring a growing team along the way.
main.result: The web app went beyond the Android app's features and lifted engagement by 30%. The logistics pivot improved operational efficiency by 40%, and system reliability rose by 25%.

privateRag.name: Private document Q&A
privateRag.summary: A self-hostable reference build for answering questions over private documents: local embeddings, a citation on every sentence, and source highlighting.

pdfAgent.name: Statement extraction agent
pdfAgent.summary: Turns bank statements and remittance PDFs into clean, validated rows, with AI proposing the mapping and deterministic checks deciding what gets through.

evalHarness.name: LLM eval harness
evalHarness.summary: A small, reusable harness for scoring model outputs against test cases and catching regressions before a prompt or model change ships.

services.title: Engineering partnerships for teams shipping AI where mistakes are expensive.
services.subtitle: Six ways I plug into a team — from a tight architectural rescue to a full 0-to-1 build — with one engineer accountable from the first whiteboard to the last deploy.

stats.sectorsValue: FinTech · B2B SaaS · AI tooling · Mobility

services.tiersSubtitle: Each service runs at the scale that matches your problem. We narrow it together on the discovery call.

micro.outcome: Architecture review, working spike, audit, or a written technical strategy you can act on.
micro.idealFor: Validating an approach before committing, second opinions, or unblocking one specific bottleneck.

mvp.scope: 1–3 months. One coherent product surface, end-to-end.
mvp.outcome: A working feature or product slice live in production, instrumented, and ready for your team to iterate on.
mvp.idealFor: Launching a new AI feature, replatforming a workflow, or building a focused 0→1 product.

enterprise.scope: 3+ months. Multiple workstreams, often with retained advisory alongside.
enterprise.outcome: A platform your team owns and operates — hardening, observability, runbooks, and handover baked in from day one.
enterprise.idealFor: Regulated rollouts, multi-team integrations, or work where mistakes are genuinely expensive.

aiIntegration.name: AI integration & architecture
aiIntegration.persona: For FinTech & B2B teams with critical legacy systems
aiIntegration.summary: Plug AI capabilities into existing production systems without putting transactions, uptime, or compliance at risk. I design parallel infrastructure that talks to your core engine instead of replacing it.
aiIntegration.included: Architecture review, threat model, isolated AI service design, eval harness for failure modes, rollout plan with rollback gates.
aiIntegration.upsells: Normally goes with: MLOps & infrastructure (Enterprise) for observability and cost controls.

secureAi.name: Secure & compliant AI deployment
secureAi.persona: For LegalTech, compliance, and regulated industries
secureAi.summary: On-prem or private-cloud AI systems for teams who can't let data phone home. Document indexing, retrieval, and summarization with full citation accuracy and an audit trail.
secureAi.included: Private RAG architecture, vector store sizing, citation/grounding evals, SOC2-friendly logging, deployment guide for your infra team.
secureAi.upsells: Normally goes with: Fractional CTO retainer for ongoing security review and pen-test triage.

aiNative.name: AI-native product engineering
aiNative.persona: For founders building 0→1 or evolving a legacy SaaS
aiNative.summary: Ship the magical UX you've been pitching the board. I build agentic workflows and AI features into the product surface — not as a chatbot bolted on the side, but as the way your product actually works.
aiNative.included: Product engineering end-to-end: data model, agent design, UI flows, instrumentation, and the unglamorous error states that make AI features feel reliable.
aiNative.upsells: Normally goes with: Agentic workflow automation when the win is on the back office, not the front-end.

agenticOps.name: Agentic workflow automation
agenticOps.persona: For ops-heavy teams in PropTech, services, and back-office
agenticOps.summary: Replace the army of analysts reading PDFs, chasing renewals, and reconciling spreadsheets. Agents that extract, flag, and draft — layered over the tools you already use, not another dashboard to log into.
agenticOps.included: Process audit, agent orchestration, integration with existing CRM/ERP, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, and ROI measurement.
agenticOps.upsells: Normally goes with: Secure & compliant AI deployment when the documents can't leave your tenancy.

mlopsRescue.name: MLOps & infrastructure rescue
mlopsRescue.persona: For Series A/B teams whose AI features are on fire
mlopsRescue.summary: Cloud bill out of control? Inference latency unacceptable? CI/CD for models doesn't exist? I come in, stop the bleeding, and leave you with a platform your team can actually operate.
mlopsRescue.included: Inference cost audit, model serving setup (vLLM/equivalent), observability for LLMs, deployment pipelines, and a written runbook for the team taking it over.
mlopsRescue.upsells: Normally goes with: AI integration & architecture if the underlying design is what's making it expensive.

fractionalCto.name: Fractional CTO & technical advisory
fractionalCto.persona: For founders without a deeply technical co-founder
fractionalCto.summary: A senior engineer in your corner for hiring, architecture decisions, vendor selection, and the board conversations where buzzwords get expensive. Retainer-based, with a fixed monthly cadence.
fractionalCto.included: Weekly working sessions, ad-hoc decision support, technical review of contractor work, hiring loops, and a written technical strategy document you can hand to investors.
fractionalCto.upsells: Normally combined with one of the build engagements above when there's a specific delivery on the line.

for.funded: You're past pre-seed — there's revenue, funding, or an enterprise contract that makes engineering quality a board-level concern.
for.regulated: You operate in regulated, high-trust, or high-stakes environments where 'move fast and break things' isn't an option.
for.legacy: You have systems that work and matter, and you need AI integrated alongside them — not a green-field rebuild.
for.scale: You've been burned by a generic AI wrapper before and now you need someone who can show you the architecture, not just the demo.

fit.notForTitle: This probably isn't a fit if

notFor.ideaGuy: You're looking for someone to build your idea for equity, or you expect a $50K MVP for $3K.
notFor.agencyMiddleman: You're a non-technical agency owner who wants to white-label senior engineering work at a junior margin.
notFor.noTechBudget: You want AI because you read about it, but your business doesn't yet have the operational maturity (or budget) to maintain software you didn't build yourself.

discovery.title: 1. Discovery
discovery.body: A free 15-minute call to understand what you're trying to ship, what's in your way, and whether I'm the right person for it. No pitch — if it's not a fit, I'll say so and point you somewhere better.

scope.title: 2. Scope & shape
scope.body: If there's a fit, I scope the work in writing: the problem, the approach, the deliverables, and the price. You see the architecture before you see an invoice.

build.title: 3. Build & ship
build.body: I work as one of your engineers — in your repos, your standups, your decision threads — until the thing is live, instrumented, and your team owns it.

cta.body: Two ways to start. Pick whichever matches where you are.
cta.principlesLink: How I think about the work

founding.label: Founding clients
founding.title: A few founding-client slots are open.
founding.body: I'm taking on a small number of founding-client engagements at a reduced rate. In exchange, we publish a short case study of the work, and you share an honest testimonial if you're happy with the result. Mention it on your discovery call.

method.title: How I work with clients
method.howToWorkParagraph1: I take on scoped consulting engagements, from focused one-to-three-week sprints to multi-quarter builds, plus fractional CTO retainers for founders who need senior technical judgment on call.
method.howToWorkParagraph2: I do my best work with teams building products where the details matter. I own problems end-to-end—from architecture and tradeoffs to the interface details users feel every day—and I leave your team able to run what we built.
method.howToWorkParagraph3: If that sounds like what you need, take the fit assessment or book a short discovery call, and we'll find out quickly whether there's a fit.
method.outro: If this resonates, I'd like to hear what you're building. Book a discovery call and I'll tell you honestly whether I'm the right person for it.

userCentric.title: user-centric
userCentric.subTitle: Design for the user, build for the impact.
userCentric.description: Impactful products solve real problems in ways that feel natural. On every engagement I start from the people using the product, not the feature list, and make sure technical decisions turn into experiences they actually notice. Expect me to ask who something is for before I ask how to build it.

quality.title: Quality
quality.subTitle: Yes, ship fast - but don't ship junk.
quality.description: Moving fast matters, but not at the cost of what you'll be maintaining next year. I build for reliability and clarity: tests where they earn their keep, observability from day one, and code your team can pick up after handover. Deadlines get met without leaving a mess behind.

collaboration.title: Collaboration
collaboration.subTitle: The best products come from diverse minds working together.
collaboration.description: I work as one of your engineers—in your repos, your standups, and your decision threads—alongside your designers and product people. Decisions are written down, tradeoffs are explained in plain language, and nobody has to chase me for a status update.

iteration.title: Iteration
iteration.subTitle: Perfection is found in iteration, not in a single release.
iteration.description: Great products come from cycles of learning and refining. I scope work so that something real ships early, gets instrumented, and tells us what to build next, instead of disappearing for months to deliver a big reveal.

simplicity.title: Simplicity
simplicity.subTitle: Simple is powerful.
simplicity.description: In both architecture and user experience, the simplest solution that works is usually the best one. I add complexity only where it pays for itself, which keeps your systems cheaper to run and easier to change long after the engagement ends.

humanCenteredAi.title: Human-Centered AI
humanCenteredAi.subTitle: Design intelligent systems that enhance the human experience.
humanCenteredAi.description: AI should make people's work better, not just look impressive in a demo. Inspired by ethical technologists like Tristan Harris and Aza Raskin, I design AI features that keep humans in control: the model proposes and explains, people decide, and every suggestion can be traced.

assessment.triagePlaybook: What happens next depends on your results. If we're a strong match, I'll usually invite you to a strategy call within one business day. If we're a good match, I'll suggest a discovery call within about two days. If you're earlier in your journey, you'll get the linked resource and one brief, helpful follow-up after about a week. If we're not the right fit right now, you won't get a sales push—I may only point you to useful reading on the site.
